senses.definition: A hot spring that sometimes shoots water and steam out of the ground.
senses.example: A geyser sent a burst of hot water up into the air.

senses.definition: A gas that contains carbon and hydrogen. In cold places such as Titan it can form liquid lakes.
senses.example: Scientists found lakes of liquid methane on Titan.

senses.definition: A kind of light that human eyes cannot see. Warm things often give off infrared light.
senses.example: Webb can collect infrared light from a cloud of dust.

senses.definition: A trip that takes a spacecraft close past an object so it can observe it.
senses.example: Voyager 2 took pictures during a flyby of Neptune.

senses.definition: A condition in which objects act as if there is very little gravity pulling them against their surroundings.
senses.example: In microgravity, an astronaut can let go of a pencil and watch it float.

senses.definition: A planet outside our solar system.
senses.example: Astronomers detected an exoplanet by watching its star become a little dimmer.

senses.definition: Kept at a set air or fluid pressure, often higher than the pressure outside.
senses.example: The inside of a space suit is pressurized so the astronaut’s body can function.

senses.definition: A huge connected body of salt water. Earth’s ocean is often divided into five named oceans.
senses.example: Waves moved across the ocean during the storm.

senses.definition: The area in which a magnet or moving electric charge can exert a magnetic force.
senses.example: A compass needle responds to Earth’s magnetic field.

senses.definition: A measure of how much matter something contains or how hard it is to change its motion.
senses.example: A full wagon has more mass than the same empty wagon.

senses.definition: A round hollow, often made where something struck a surface or around the opening of a volcano.
senses.example: The large crater on the Moon has high sides.

senses.definition: Water in its gas form.
senses.example: Water vapor in the warm air turned into little drops on the window.

senses.definition: A gas that makes up most of Earth’s air and is found in many living things.
senses.example: The air we breathe contains nitrogen as well as oxygen.

senses.definition: A scientist who studies rocks and what they show about a world’s past.
senses.example: The geologist used marks inside the rock to tell how it had formed.

senses.definition: The distance light can travel in one year, about 9.5 trillion kilometers.
senses.example: The next star is more than four light-years from the Sun.

senses.definition: The boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing can escape to the outside.
senses.example: Light that passes inside the event horizon cannot come back out.

senses.definition: The bending of a wave as it enters something where it moves at a different speed.
senses.example: Refraction can make a straw look bent near the surface of a glass of water.

senses.definition: The way light or sound bounces off a surface.
senses.example: I saw my reflection in the still water.

senses.definition: A thin thread of glass or plastic that carries light along it.
senses.example: A small pulse of light can travel a long way inside a fiber optic.

senses.definition: The movement of heat or electricity through something, such as through a metal spoon.
senses.example: The spoon handle warmed by conduction after the bowl of the spoon touched the soup.

senses.definition: The way a gas or liquid carries heat as it moves from place to place.
senses.example: Convection carried warmer water toward the top of the pot.

senses.definition: Energy sent out in waves or particles. Light is a kind of radiation.
senses.example: Radiation from the Sun can travel through empty space.

senses.definition: A wheel with blades that spins when flowing water, air or steam pushes on it.
senses.example: Moving water turned a turbine inside the dam.

senses.definition: A machine that makes electricity, often by spinning wires or magnets.
senses.example: The wind turbine turned a generator that sent electricity to homes.

senses.definition: A device that turns energy from light straight into electricity.
senses.example: Many small photovoltaic cells can make up one solar panel.

senses.definition: Energy supplied by heat from inside Earth.
senses.example: Warm water brought up from underground can supply geothermal energy.

senses.definition: A way to find objects or measure distance using sound, often under water.
senses.example: The crew used sonar to make a map of the seafloor.

senses.definition: A tiny part of matter with a negative electric charge. Electrons are found around the centers of atoms.
senses.example: Electrons can move through the copper wire in a circuit.

senses.definition: The main physical forms matter can take, including solid, liquid and gas.
senses.example: Ice, liquid water and water vapor are three states of matter.

senses.definition: A sound that returns after bouncing off a surface.
senses.example: I heard an echo when I called across the valley.

senses.definition: A place where water is collected and stored, often behind a dam.
senses.example: The reservoir held rainwater for the dry months.

senses.definition: A measure of the difference in electric energy per unit of charge between two places. It can help drive electric current.
senses.example: The small battery has a lower voltage than the source of power for a house.

senses.definition: A machine that makes a part move using power from electricity, fuel or another source.
senses.example: An electric motor turned the fan’s blades.

senses.definition: A push that moves a vehicle forward or in a chosen direction.
senses.example: Thrust from the propeller helped push the airplane forward.

senses.definition: A force, often from moving air, that acts across the direction of motion and can hold an aircraft up.
senses.example: The glider’s wings made enough lift to stay in the air.

senses.definition: A force from a fluid such as air or water that opposes movement through it.
senses.example: Drag made it harder to ride my bike into the wind.

senses.definition: The upward push that a liquid or gas gives to something in it.
senses.example: The buoyancy of the water helped hold the boat up.

senses.definition: A tank that can hold water or air to change how a boat or submarine floats.
senses.example: Water entered the ballast tank as the submarine went deeper.

senses.definition: A part that fits closely inside a tube and moves back and forth when a liquid or gas pushes on it.
senses.example: Steam pushed the piston, which helped move a train’s wheels.

senses.definition: A machine part that spins, such as the blades on top of a helicopter.
senses.example: The helicopter’s rotor pushed air downward.

senses.definition: Small pieces of sand, clay or other material that settle after moving through water or air.
senses.example: A layer of sediment gathered at the bottom of the pond.

senses.definition: A force that acts between touching surfaces to resist sliding, or that can stop them from starting to slide.
senses.example: Friction between the tires and the road helped the bicycle turn.

senses.definition: A wheel with teeth that fit into openings in a chain.
senses.example: The pedals turn a sprocket that pulls the bicycle chain.

senses.definition: A toothed wheel that moves another toothed part and can change speed, force or direction.
senses.example: The small gear turned quickly when the big wheel drove it.

senses.definition: Small hard balls and the rings that guide them, allowing parts of a machine to roll past each other smoothly.
senses.example: The wheel used a ball bearing to turn around its axle.

senses.definition: A piece with a narrow edge that can push things apart or hold something in place.
senses.example: A rubber wedge held the door open.

senses.definition: A rod on which a wheel turns or that turns with a wheel.
senses.example: The wheels of the toy truck spun around a metal axle.

senses.definition: The use of a liquid under pressure to move things or apply a force.
senses.example: A lift in the garage uses hydraulics to raise a car.

senses.definition: A weight used to balance another weight or make it easier to move around.
senses.example: A counterweight balances much of the weight of the elevator car.

senses.definition: An object hung so that it can swing to and fro.
senses.example: The clock’s pendulum swung back and forth.

senses.definition: The point that describes where an object’s mass is balanced. It may fall in an empty space within the object.
senses.example: The center of mass of the ring was in the middle of its open space.

senses.definition: The angle between the direction a compass points locally and the direction to Earth’s geographic north pole.
senses.example: A map showed the magnetic declination for the area so we could compare the needle with true north.

senses.definition: Spinning once for every trip around a neighboring body, so one side stays facing that body.
senses.example: The Moon’s synchronous rotation keeps nearly the same side facing Earth.

senses.definition: A streak of light made when a small object speeds through a planet’s atmosphere.
senses.example: We saw a bright meteor streak across the night sky.

senses.definition: A piece of rock or metal from space that reaches the ground after traveling through an atmosphere.
senses.example: The museum showed a meteorite that landed in a farmer’s field.

senses.definition: A flow of tiny charged particles that keeps blowing outward from the Sun.
senses.example: The solar wind carries pieces of the Sun’s outer atmosphere out into space.

senses.definition: A glow in a planet’s upper atmosphere caused by particles giving energy to a gas there.
senses.example: An aurora looked like a green curtain over the dark hills.

senses.definition: An enormous cloud of gas, dust or both in space.
senses.example: Young stars were forming inside the cloudy nebula.

senses.definition: The hot, compact center left behind after a star like the Sun loses its outside layers.
senses.example: A white dwarf can glow for a very long time after a star stops using its fuel.

senses.definition: A very dense object left when the center of some massive stars collapses.
senses.example: A spinning neutron star can send a beam that appears to flash from Earth.

senses.definition: A huge explosion of a star or of certain remains of a star.
senses.example: The supernova grew bright enough for astronomers to see from very far away.

senses.definition: Either of the two moments each year when a hemisphere tilts farthest toward or away from the Sun.
senses.example: Near the June solstice, summer days are longest in places north of the equator.

senses.definition: Either of the two moments each year when Earth’s poles are tilted neither toward nor away from the Sun.
senses.example: Around the equinox, day and night at many places are almost the same length.

senses.definition: The lightest chemical element, made of atoms whose centers have one proton. It is found in water and in stars.
senses.example: In the center of the Sun, hydrogen helps supply the star’s energy.

senses.definition: Energy that moves from a warmer object or place to a cooler one because of that difference in temperature.
senses.example: Heat moved from the hot soup into the metal spoon.
